Plan, not record. September 2026 has not happened. This is what the planner would do, day by day, produced by the simulator that backtested August to within a fraction of a percent. Forecast demand is marked FORECAST; every declared assumption is flagged in the data. WhatsApp messages are simulated drafts — nothing was sent, nobody replied.

Lines PLAN

6 filling lines, 12 h shifts, 26 working days (4 Sundays off). 339 planned runs would fill 27,65,370 L. A line takes any oil — only the pack size ties a SKU to a machine. None of this has been run.

open question Q4blockingaffects every hour on this page

“Do the filling lines actually stop around 16:20, or do they keep running to about 19:00 with the output keyed in once at the end of the run?”

Every hour here is charged against the simulator’s 12-hour working day. Until Q4 is answered, that clock is an assumption ASSUMED — if the lines really run later than the plan’s day, the utilisation and idle-hour figures move with the answer.

What the plan fills at

Two slots are derated twice — say it right

Most slots carry a rated speed, and the sim plans them at 50% of it — the derate the August backtest calibrated (replayed on August, the engine landed 21,22,639 L against 21,19,237 L actually made) ASSUMED. But Clear Pack 5L and Tin Head TIN are stored at rates someone watched the line do — and the plan derates those by 50% again. So their planned pace is the observed rate, then 50% efficiency — not 50% of rated:

Clear Pack 5L
1,000 pcs/hr observed → plan runs 500 pcs/hr
Tin Head TIN
215 pcs/hr observed → plan runs 108 pcs/hr

Data register: every stored rate is multiplied by this efficiency in the plan; for the two slots stored at OBSERVED rates (Clear Pack 5L, Tin Head) that is a second derate on top of observation — the honest phrasing is 'observed rate, then 50% efficiency'

The Clear Pack 15L, 10 Head 15L, 6 Head 15L rates are DERIVED — no measured rate exists for that pack, so the sim declares the assumption instead of inventing a speed. A slot missing from a line means that pack size is not set up there.

The changeover bill — time, not material

Changeover time
270.1 h
16,204 min — 16% of time on the lines

22.5
full 12-hour line-days of switching
Oil changes
231
+ 24 pack-size-only clearances
Flush oil cycled
92,400 L
400 L per change — run through and REUSED, not consumed

The rule the sim charges: an oil change costs TIME not material: 400 L of the next oil is run through and reused, plus 51.3 min clearance; a pack-size change on the same oil costs the 51.3 min clearance only. So the flush is not a material cost — the 400 L of the next oil comes back — but every switch still pays its minutes, and 231 oil changes add up to 270.1 hours the lines aren’t filling.

What no line can do: nothing here is configured for a DRUM or 3L slot, so 4 plan SKUs — 66,000 L of the month’s plan — cannot be produced at all. They are not hidden in the bars above; they never reach a line. See them on Materials →

This is a forward plan, not a record. September 2026 has not happened; only the 1-September opening is observed. The factory has not run this way.
Measured: the 31-Aug stock and open POs, the open order backlog, BOMs, line speeds and clearance, realise, lead times. Assumed (declared, flagged in the data): forecast demand buckets for volume not yet ordered, the even ecom spread, supply exactly on lead time, the invoice→truck lag, the observed line-efficiency derate, the storage ceiling (open question Q2), standing stock uncounted at open. Phone numbers are masked — September has no approval to show them.
Every number traces to sim/sep-inputs.json via scripts/gen-data.py.
